notes: Both ketiv/qere units are underdetermined and carry no exclusion mark, so the prepared projection is aligned as given (rules 9, 53).

פְּלִילִים takes the whole recast relational expression *to be punished by the judges*, headed on the noun that writes its lexeme (rules 19, 24): the bare preposition cannot state the relation on its own here, so dropping the participle leaves no grammatical rendering. The materially different reading is rule 20's nominal-recasting boundary (*violence done to the land*), which would mark *to be punished* `added` and leave *by the judges* to the rectum; that ruling turns on a dispensable participle beside an already adequate *violence ... to the land*, which is not this shape.
*a heinous crime* heads on *heinous* by rule 31's subtraction, since *crime* alone is any crime; heading on *crime* was the competing reading.
